title: Rounded lips: /w/
goal: Practise /w/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Round your lips, then move smoothly into the next vowel. Your upper teeth do not need to touch your lower lip, as they do for v.
spelling: w often represents /w/. In write, the w is silent; learn the whole word as well as the pattern.
task: Ask where to wait. Listen, then repeat the instruction in your own voice.
story: The road is wet. We wait by the window.

articulation.label: wet
articulation.alt: wet: /w/ → /ɛ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /w/: Round the lips; raise the back of the tongue.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: A round part of a vehicle that turns as it moves. A bike has two wheels.
one vertical side of a room or building. A window is on the back wall.
look at something for a period of time. Mia and Puck watch a movie at seven.
move on your feet at a normal speed. Mia walks to the store.
an adult female person. A woman and a man are by the door.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
